title: Masseur-initiated cancellation of an already-confirmed booking
tech: Node/TypeScript backend (new route/service/email template) + a small React frontend addition to the existing AdminDashboard
keyConstraints: This is a known gap flagged since the original design doc: the masseur can decline a pending request (pending -> cancelled), but has no way to cancel a booking they already confirmed on their own initiative -- e.g. they made a mistake, or something came up. Critical routing detail, confirmed by reading routes/bookings.ts: the path `POST /bookings/:id/cancel` is ALREADY taken by the customer's token-based self-service cancel route (task 007) -- this new masseur-facing action must live at a DIFFERENT path, `POST /admin/bookings/:id/cancel`, matching the existing `/admin/bookings` prefix convention (GET /admin/bookings) and authenticated the same way (requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit), never a query-string token. Scope this strictly to bookings currently in 'confirmed' status -- do not let it also apply to 'pending' bookings, since decline already owns that transition with its own distinct customer email ('could not be accommodated'); allowing two different code paths to cancel a pending booking would be confusing and redundant. Reuse the existing declineBookingSchema as-is for the request body (optional reason, 1-500 chars, trimmed) -- no new validation file needed, the shape is identical.
description: Add a masseur-only action to cancel a booking that's already in 'confirmed' status. Backend: add a `transitionConfirmedBooking` helper in bookingService.ts, mirroring the existing `transitionPendingBooking` pattern exactly (same conditional-UPDATE-then-diagnose-why-it-matched-nothing shape) but with `WHERE status = 'confirmed'` instead of 'pending' -- on no match, look up the booking to distinguish BookingNotFoundError (404) from a new BookingNotConfirmedError (409, mirroring the existing BookingNotPendingError's exact shape) for a booking that exists but isn't confirmed (e.g. already cancelled, or still pending). Add `cancelBookingForAdmin(id, reason)` using this helper, defaulting cancellationReason to 'cancelled by masseur' when no reason is given (unlike declineBooking, which allows a genuinely null reason -- here a customer whose CONFIRMED appointment just got pulled deserves at least a generic explanation, since they have no other signal that anything happened). Add a new EmailJobType 'booking_cancelled_by_masseur' with its own template in emailTemplates.ts (distinct tone from renderCancelledByCustomer -- this is the masseur cancelling on a customer who was expecting to show up, not the customer's own request, so the copy should read like an apology/notice, e.g. 'We're sorry, but your confirmed appointment for X on Y has had to be cancelled.') and a corresponding enqueueBookingCancelledByMasseur in emailQueueService.ts (same BookingEmailPayload shape and manageUrl/token-minting pattern as the other customer-facing booking emails). Add the route POST /admin/bookings/:id/cancel (requireMasseurAuth, adminRateLimit, declineBookingSchema for the body) returning { id, status, cancelled_at, cancellation_reason } -- identical response shape to the existing decline response, so the frontend can reuse the same response type. Frontend: in AdminDashboard.tsx, add a 'Cancel booking' action visible only when booking.status === 'confirmed' (pending already has Confirm/Decline; cancelled is terminal), using the exact same two-step confirm UX already established for Decline (optional reason textarea, 'Confirm cancel' / 'Never mind' buttons) -- add a new client.ts function (name it distinctly from the existing token-based customer `cancelBooking`, e.g. `cancelBookingAsAdmin`, to avoid confusion between the two completely different auth models) that calls the new admin route via the existing authRequest/Bearer pattern.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /admin/bookings/:id/cancel requires a valid masseur session (401 without one, matching every other /admin/* route) and lives at a distinct path from the customer's token-based POST /bookings/:id/cancel -- the two must not collide or share a route handler

Only a 'confirmed' booking can be cancelled through this action -- attempting it on a 'pending' or already-'cancelled' booking returns 409 (BookingNotConfirmedError), and a nonexistent booking id returns 404, matching the existing transitionPendingBooking error-diagnosis pattern
On success, the booking's status becomes 'cancelled', cancelled_at is set, and cancellation_reason defaults to 'cancelled by masseur' when no reason was supplied in the request body

A new booking_cancelled_by_masseur email is enqueued to the customer with a fresh minted token and manage link, using copy that reads as the masseur cancelling on the customer (not the customer's own request) -- distinct from both booking_declined and booking_cancelled_by_customer's existing copy
AdminDashboard.tsx shows a 'Cancel booking' action only for bookings with status 'confirmed', using the same explicit two-step confirm pattern already used for Decline -- not a bare window.confirm()
The dashboard list updates the row in place on success (status flips to 'cancelled'), no full reload, matching the existing confirm/decline behavior
A 401 on this new action follows the existing onSessionEnded flow like every other authenticated dashboard action

New backend unit/integration test coverage for cancelBookingForAdmin and the route (success, wrong-status 409, nonexistent-id 404, missing auth 401, default reason when none supplied), plus frontend test coverage for the new dashboard action mirroring the existing Decline tests
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/pages/AdminDashboard.tsx (add the Cancel action for confirmed bookings)
frontend/src/api/types.ts (reuse or extend the existing decline response type)
securityConsiderations: Same authorization model as every other admin mutation (requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit) -- no new auth pattern introduced. The new route must not be reachable or confusable with the customer's token-based cancel route at a different path; keep the two completely separate in both routing and service-layer logic (cancelBookingForAdmin takes no token, cancelBookingForCustomer's customerHasAccess check must not be touched or reused here). Reuses the existing token-minting (mintCustomerToken) and manage-link pattern already reviewed for every other customer-facing booking email -- no new token model.
